extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, patent policy analysts, USPTO/patent office staff, and economists studying patenting behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical evaluation of continuation-filings (CAP, CIP, divisional, combination) and their correlates using patent-, firm-, and technology-level metrics to inform patent policy and continuation reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation type taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of continuations into CAP, CIP, Divisional, Combination (and 'ordinary' non-continued patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout tables and figures (e.g., TABLE 1, Figure 1) to report incidence (% of continued patents) by priority/grant year and technology; forms the primary categorical outcome in multinomial logit models (dependent variable: continuation type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of claims per patent (reported by continuation type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a descriptive characteristic of patents in TABLE 2 and A3.1; differences across continuation types and technologies are interpreted as an attribute associated with continuation usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of backward citations listed in a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by continuation type and technology (TABLE 2, A3.2) as an indicator of prior-art reliance and to control for patent context in regressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: % Selfcites (Backward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of backward citations that are self-citations (applicant/firm self-citation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High % self-cites (CAP applicants disproportionately cite their own previous patents) is interpreted as evidence consistent with defensive patenting; reported in TABLE 2 and A3.3 and used to characterize CAP behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Originality" metric
rubrics_metrics.description: "Originality" (quoted as used by the authors) reported for patents by continuation type and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a descriptive/analysis variable (TABLE 2, A3.4). The paper notes regressions including an 'originality' regression with significant backward-cites control; values and comparisons are used to infer novelty differences across continuation types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward Citations (FCITES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-year forward citation counts used as a measure of patent 'quality' or importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used extensively as an explanatory/interaction variable in probit and multinomial logit models (e.g., FCITES, FCITES*lnRDINT*lnPATINT). The paper uses fcites to proxy patent value and tests how fcites interact with firm- and patent-level intensity measures to predict continuation types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability of expiry at 4 years (Pr. of expiry at 4 yrs.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated probability that a patent will have expired by 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by continuation type (TABLE 2, A3.6) as an outcome/indicator of patent economic value and maintenance behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency period and number of continuation filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Pendency (time in prosecution) and count of continuation filings per application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in TABLE A1 (Mean and Median). Number of continuation filings and pendency are used to profile continuation behavior (e.g., CAPs show different mean/median continuation filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-inserted vs. applicant-inserted backward citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Share/median of examiner-inserted backward citations vs applicant-inserted citations (reported for patents issued 2001-2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TABLE A2.1 reports median cites and median % of examiner cites by continuation type; differences inform interpretations about applicant behavior and examiner influence on cited prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent intensity (lnPATINT)
rubrics_metrics.description: log patenting intensity (patents per M$ R&D); variable labeled lnPATINT in models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as an explanatory variable in multinomial logit and other models (TABLES 6, 7, A5) to capture firms' patenting rate; changes in lnPATINT affect probabilities of different continuation types.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D intensity (lnRDINT)
rubrics_metrics.description: log R&D intensity (M$ / 1000 employees); variable labeled lnRDINT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an explanatory variable and in interactions (e.g., lnRDINT*lnPATINT) to assess how firm investment intensity relates to continuation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital intensity (lnCAPINT)
rubrics_metrics.description: log capital intensity (M$ of property, plant, & equipment / 1000 employees); variable labeled lnCAPINT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in models and interacted with lnPATINT to test how capital intensity correlates with continuation type choices (TABLES 6, 7, A5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction terms among patent/firm intensity and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Interaction variables such as lnRDINT*lnPATINT, lnCAPINT*lnPATINT, FCITES*lnRDINT*lnPATINT, FCITES*lnCAPINT*lnPATINT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interaction terms are key model dimensions (TABLES 6, 7, A5). Signs and significance of these coefficients are interpreted (TABLE 4) to infer whether continuations are used by technology traders, defensive patenters, or technology specialists for more/less important patents; triple interactions incorporate patent quality (fcites).

rubrics_metrics.name: TECHSHARE (share of patents from primary class)
rubrics_metrics.description: TechShare: the share of a firm's patents coming from the primary (technology) class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in multinomial models as a control/explanatory variable to account for technological specialization's effect on continuation choices (TABLE 6 and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: TECHTIME (technology lag)
rubrics_metrics.description: TechTime: priority year minus first priority year in technology class (a measure of technology lag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a covariate in models to capture timing/experience in the technology area (TABLES 6, 7, A7.x panels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm size and age (employment, age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Log employment (firm size) and log age (firm age) included as model covariates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in descriptive statistics (TABLE 5) and included in models (TABLES 6, 7) as controls for firm characteristics affecting continuation behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation framework for interaction coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLE 4: mapping of coefficient sign combinations to implied types of continuation users and hypotheses (e.g., technology traders, defensive patenters, technology specialists for important/less valuable patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit rubric for inferring behavioral motives from regression coefficient signs: e.g., positive β(RDINT X PATINT) suggests 'technology traders'; positive β(CAPINT X PATINT) suggests 'defensive patenters'; FCITES interaction signs distinguish 'technology specialists' for important vs less valuable patents; overall mapping used to support hypotheses ('Pioneering inventors' vs 'defensive patenting').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multinomial logit / probit modeling practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Modeling choices: dependent variable = continuation type (base class: no continuation j=0); inclusion of industry-, technology-, and patent vintage-effects; standard errors in brackets; significance indicated with * at 1%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the methodological/reporting standards used in the paper's empirical analysis (TABLES 6, 7, A6, etc.); signals how statistical evidence is judged and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy reform proposal: showing for subsequent continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule (Official Gazette of the USPTO 2006): require second or subsequent continuations of an application to 'include a showing as to why the amendment, argument, or evidence presented could not have been previously submitted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note such petitions might impose additional burdens on the PTO but could aid examiners in evaluating CIPs more effectively; they also state their results 'undermine the case for the "Continuation Application."' This is presented as a specific procedural criterion for continuation filings under reform discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy recommendation: reexamine CAP benefits and monitor CIP links
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to reexamine purported benefits of the CAP and to monitor links among patent value, firm characteristics, and litigation for patents issuing from CIPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors argue skepticism concerning CAP benefits is warranted and suggest that continuation process reform should be informed by closer monitoring of how continuation-origin patents relate to value, firm traits, and later litigation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive reporting conventions and sample construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting descriptive statistics (median, mean, SD, min, max) for firm- and patent-level variables and sample sizes (e.g., N of observations; priority year windows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper documents conventions (e.g., standard errors in brackets, grouping years into application periods 1981-85, 86-90, 91-95, 95-2000) that affect inference about continuity of results and robustness checks; these are practical standards for empirical presentation.
